method: Claude's rating: crowd score weighted by review volume, plus awards and guide listings, spread onto a 5-star scale.

venues.name: The Lough Ree Inn
venues.note: Lakeside pub and bistro at Coosan Point with lake views, a playground and swimming nearby; new management. Beef and lamb come from the owners' own farm and the burger is praised, but food reviews are mixed. Daily specials and afternoon tea. No website or published hours; ring ahead.

venues.name: Wineport Lodge
venues.note: Luxury lakeside lodge and spa with its own jetty for diners: excellent food, a friendly bar, superb lake views and special-occasion service; Sunday lunch is popular but on the pricey side. Taste of the Waterways award 2020. Hours not published online; ring or book a table.

venues.name: Glasson Lakehouse
venues.note: Modern lakeside hotel with its own marina and grounds: Bonnie's restaurant serves lunch and dinner daily and Tom's pub serves food from midday to late. Food is well liked; service can be stretched when busy. Live music some Sunday afternoons.
venues.where: Glasson (Bonnie's restaurant, Tom's Fish & Tackle pub)

venues.name: Killinure Chalets
venues.note: Lively bar-restaurant renowned for its steaks and steak sandwich, cooked just right. No bookings for food: expect a wait, up to two hours at busy times, with a drink at the bar. Ring ahead to ask where you can tie up; Quigleys Marina next door doesn't allow hire boats.

venues.name: Hodson Bay Hotel
venues.note: Large lakeside hotel on Hodson Bay with its own jetty: hotel dining with friendly, attentive staff, live music in the bar some evenings, and food much praised at functions. L'Escale dinner hours not published; book ahead.

venues.name: Coffeys
venues.note: Fourth-generation pub and grocery (est. 1918), truly authentic and beautifully kept, with an off-licence, near Lecarrow Harbour: warm welcome, superb Guinness, coffee, pizza some evenings and music sessions on summer Wednesdays. Go for the pub.

venues.name: Sorrento
venues.note: Family-run Italian restaurant on Main Street, widely rated the best food in the area: tiger prawns, sea bass with asparagus tempura, stuffed chicken, beef escalope and a good Italian wine list; big plates at fair prices. Fills up, so book. Few vegetarian or vegan dishes.

venues.name: LanesBrew Coffee Shop
venues.note: Friendly coffee shop on Main Street with benches outside and a private room: excellent Calendar coffee, almond croissants, sausage rolls, banana bread, home bakes, bubble tea and açaí bowls.

venues.name: Adies Bar & Restaurant
venues.note: Family-run bar and restaurant on Main Street (also known as Farrell's) with rooms above and live music at weekends: good-value bar food at lunch and dinner in big portions, though one reviewer found the fish poor. Friendly staff. Hours not on its own site.

venues.name: The Swan Tavern
venues.note: Friendly local pub sharing a kitchen and phone with Adies: lunches full every day with families and farmers, big portions at fair prices, Irish beef praised, an excellent pint, a heated dog-friendly courtyard and frequent live music.

venues.name: Ping's Oriental Take Away
venues.note: Chinese takeaway by the bridge: honey shredded chicken and salt and pepper chicken are liked; reviews are split on portions and quality. Closed Monday and Tuesday.

venues.name: Tasty Kebab & Pizza
venues.note: Takeaway for pizza, kebabs and burgers. Boaters praise quick, friendly service and good pizza (double pepperoni); other reviewers had poor food or wrong orders.

venues.name: Village Inn Take Away
venues.note: Takeaway with a thin-base pizza that locals rate highly; also chips, biryani and milkshakes. The fish and doner get poor reviews.

venues.name: The Yacht Bar
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Family-run local, comfortable and friendly, with a great pint, the races on and a warm welcome for visitors.

venues.name: The Purple Onion
venues.note: Lively restaurant by the bridge, among the best on the Shannon, reviewers say: seafood landed daily at Killybegs, Monaghan Wagyu, rump of lamb, fish tacos, home baking such as the bakewell tart; music and great service. Taste of the Waterways award 2024. Popular; book a table.

venues.name: Keenan's
venues.note: Landmark pub, restaurant and boutique hotel by the bridge, with a cosy bar, a conservatory and a brighter room out the back; busy at lunch, so book. Compact menu done well: the garlic steak sandwich is famous, also Thai green curry, chicken dishes, soup and toasties. Day menu 12:00–17:00 Mon–Sat, evening 17:00–20:30 Mon–Sat, Sunday menu 12:00–19:30 (its own menus page, Nov 2026). Taste of the Waterways award 2011.

venues.name: Richmond Inn
venues.note: Family-run pub with rooms overlooking the harbour where the Shannon, Camlin and Royal Canal meet: friendly locals, a good pint and a slightly dated, homely bar. Hearty home cooking: vol-au-vents, steak sandwich, lamb stew, breaded plaice, Sunday roast. Traditional Irish food seven days a week, occasional live music.
